answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small bond that only unlocks after peers attest real work, like a wharf charging mooring fees before a ship may unload. Newcomers start on a narrow ledge: limited throughput until their attestations accumulate, so one operator spinning up a thousand clones pays a thousand bonds and still waits in the same slow queue. A single thread of verified history — who attested whom, and when — makes the clone farm visible, because cheap identities share the same thin past while genuine ones diverge.
